title: Modeling and Simulation Credibility Assessment of Explicit Finite Element Analyses for Total Knee Replacement Wear and Contact Mechanics
runhead: Credibility of Explicit FEA for TKR Wear/Contact
device: Posterior-stabilized total knee replacement with metallic femoral component, UHMWPE tibial insert, and metallic tibial baseplate

models.name: GEX-WEAR: Generic Explicit Tibiofemoral Contact–Wear Model
models.what_it_computes: Transient tibiofemoral contact pressures, slip velocities, cross-shear, and volumetric wear using a rate-form wear law with cross-shear dependence; includes nonlinear UHMWPE response, surface friction, and backside insert–baseplate contact for fretting assessment

models.name: PSM-XL: Patient-Specific Malalignment and Laxity Explicit Knee Model
models.what_it_computes: Dynamic contact mechanics under imposed malalignment and ligamentous laxity using explicit penalty contact; computes edge-load contact stress fields, lift-off, third-body abrasive wear contribution, and patellofemoral-tibiofemoral load transfer during demanding maneuvers

mechanisms.name: Steady-cycle tibiofemoral surface wear under gait
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Volumetric wear and cross-linked UHMWPE damage drive debris generation and long-term osteolysis risk

mechanisms.name: Edge loading from varus–valgus malalignment and laxity
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Localized stress concentrations and lift-off promote surface damage, delamination, and premature failure

mechanisms.name: Cross-shear–accelerated wear in deep flexion pivot
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High posterior contact pressures with multidirectional sliding amplify wear in activities requiring kneeling or pivot turns

mechanisms.name: Backside fretting at the insert–baseplate interface
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Micromotion and fretting at non-articular interfaces contribute to backside wear and particulate generation

deviation.detail: Per-factor credibility is scored on a 0–12 index (12 best) for each model × mechanism; composite scores are geometric means across factors
